title: How societies choose brass bands
summary: Bands do not give samples; society members know every band. Henry points to people who keep the society records.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: There's something else I was wondering about now. Say, do you ever hear of brass bands giving a sample to anybody? Say the Widow or somebody or the club? Give them what? A sample of the music. No.
Before they hired, yeah. To give them an idea how they sound.
No. No, since I've been playing.
So they find out about the brass bands another way then?

Well, yeah, but I'm going to tell you, in a way, they knows all the brass bands. Oh, since. They got all the society and things around there. They got men in there who know every band in the age around there, you see. They have some men in society that used to be an old musician, you understand? So they know, you see. You can't fool them a bit. They know the best and the worst, they know the worst.
And even if they weren't, they probably grew up as second liners. I mean, they've heard them all their lives, I guess.
Yeah, I see. They've heard them all their lives. That's right.
I'd like to talk to some of those guys from the society who helped to choose the band, you know, and stuff. If you can get any of them's names or addresses.

But I tell you, the best way you can get there, you see Ray or Paiso or the other person where you see them, they keep all that. But we all, we don't worry about that. We just worry about the guy's job. If you call the upteller, you meet, see the person even going on. But otherwise, we don't worry about it, see.
